title: The board and the pieces
intro: Start here if you are new to chess. Meet the board, learn how squares are named, and find out what each piece is worth.

lessons.title: The chessboard
lessons.summary: Ranks, files and the name of every square.

steps.title: Welcome to chess
steps.text: A short video will welcome you here. For now, your coach shows you around the board.
This is how every game starts. White's pieces are at the bottom and Black's at the top. White always moves first.
The rows going across are called ranks. They are numbered 1 to 8, starting from White's side. Here is the 4th rank.
The columns going up are called files. They are lettered a to h, from White's left. Here is the e-file.
Every square is named by its file letter, then its rank number. This square is e4, and the white king stands on e1.
Move your king one square up, to e2.
steps.hint: Find the e-file, then count up to rank 2.
steps.ifWrong: That is not e2. The square straight above the king is e2.

steps.hint: The d-file is just left of the e-file.
steps.ifWrong: Not quite. d1 is on the bottom rank, one file to the left.

steps.hint: The f-file is right of the e-file; rank 2 is one up.
steps.ifWrong: Not quite. f2 is one square up and one to the right.

lessons.title: The pieces and their values
lessons.summary: Six kinds of piece, and what each one is worth.

steps.text: The king is the most important piece. If your king is trapped (checkmate), you lose the game.
The queen is the strongest piece. Each side starts with one, next to the king.
Rooks stand in the corners, knights next to them, and bishops next to the king and queen.
In front stand eight pawns. They are the smallest pieces, but they can grow into a queen, as you will see later.
Pieces have rough values in pawns: pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9. The king cannot be traded, so it has no value. Use these numbers to decide what to capture.
Your rook can capture a knight or a queen. Take the more valuable piece.
steps.hint: The queen is worth 9, the knight only 3.
steps.ifWrong: Look again: which black piece is worth the most?
steps.ifRight: Right! A queen is worth 9 pawns.

feedback.d4d7: That wins a knight (3), but the queen (9) was there for the taking.

steps.text: Your bishop can capture a pawn or a rook. Which is worth more?
steps.ifWrong: Look again: which black piece is worth the most?

feedback.c4b5: That wins a pawn (1). The rook (5) is worth much more.
